speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty speaking, swallowing, or noticing any changes in your vision or balance? I also need to know if you have experienced any recent fevers, night sweats, or pain in your neck or shoulder region.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine
Given the focal neurological deficits and significant weight loss, I need to rule out structural lesions like a tumor or severe disc herniation in your cervical spine.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the cervical spine MRI is normal, I need to investigate peripheral causes like diabetes-related neuropathy or steroid-induced myopathy. Do you have any weakness or sensory changes in your left arm, and have you noticed any muscle wasting or tremors in the affected right arm?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the significant weight loss and heavy smoking history, I need to rule out a Pancoast tumor causing a brachial plexus lesion. REQUEST TEST: Chest_CT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest CT confirms a solid mass at the apex of the right lung, which is highly suggestive of a Pancoast tumor compressing the brachial plexus. This explains your right arm weakness, sensory loss, pain, and significant weight loss. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor
